sheet.name: Approaching a positive historic record
sheet.definition: the press presents the followed player as able to equal or break a notable record in his next game.
sheet.inclusionCriteria: a dated article, published before the game, presents the record as within reach in that game; the record is individual (a league record, a record of his team's history, or a career milestone the press presents as historic).
sheet.exclusionCriteria: a team record; a record already broken; a statistical curiosity no outlet presents before the game; the following games, when the record is not broken in the first game presented as decisive, because a record gives only one event.
sheet.datingRule: the first publication that presents the record as within reach in the next game.
sheet.genericExample: the day before a game, a national outlet writes that player A is only a few points short of the scoring record of team X's history.

sheet.name: Public humiliation
sheet.definition: a public act or remark, by an identifiable author, that belittles or ridicules the followed player by name.
sheet.inclusionCriteria: the act or remark targets the player by name; it belittles him (mockery, contempt, doubt cast on his worth or status, a derisive gesture); its author is identifiable by role (opponent, coach, his own included, executive, media outlet, commentator); it is reported by at least one dated press article.
sheet.exclusionCriteria: criticism of a specific play in an ordinary game analysis; an anonymous social-media message the press does not report; a play suffered on the court, unless an identified author then mocks it publicly; racist remarks (type "Racist abuse"); a hostile exchange between the player and another player (type "Conflict between players"); a wave of criticism from several outlets with no single triggering remark (type "Media storm").
sheet.datingRule: the moment the remark or act becomes public (live broadcast, publication), established by the first dated article that reports it.
sheet.genericExample: the day before a game, the coach of team X says at a press conference that player A is not at the level of a top player; a national outlet reports it that evening; the measured game is player A's game the next day.

sheet.name: Media storm
sheet.definition: a wave of negative coverage centered on the followed player, triggered by an identifiable public fact: a statement, a behavior, a controversy about his commitment.
sheet.inclusionCriteria: a public, dated triggering fact; critical articles from at least three distinct outlets within two days (the sheet's coverage threshold); the player is at the center of the coverage.
sheet.exclusionCriteria: an isolated critical remark (type "Public humiliation"); a conflict with another player (type "Conflict between players"); a racist incident (type "Racist abuse"); a controversy touching the player's private life or health.
sheet.datingRule: the moment the coverage threshold is reached, that is the publication of the article that crosses it; one triggering fact gives only one event.
sheet.genericExample: after a statement by player A judged offhand, three national outlets publish critical articles about his commitment within two days; the measured game is player A's first game after the third article.

sheet.name: Racist abuse
sheet.definition: the followed player is the target of racist remarks, gestures or messages reported by the press.
sheet.inclusionCriteria: the press reports that the player was personally targeted; the author is designated by role (spectator, opponent, public figure, author of online messages); the incident is dated.
sheet.exclusionCriteria: a general racist climate with no incident targeting the player; the player speaking about racism in general, with no incident targeting him; an incident targeting another player.
sheet.datingRule: if the incident happened during a game, it is public from that moment, and the measured game is the next game; otherwise the date is that of the first dated article that reports it.
sheet.genericExample: during an away game, a spectator shouts racist insults at player A; a national outlet reports it the next day; the measured game is player A's next game.
